cues.en: Another thing we can measure is churn.
cues.zh: 另一項可以衡量的是推薦變動率，也就是 churn。

cues.en: How often do the recommendations for a user change?
cues.zh: 某位使用者的推薦，多常會改變？

cues.en: In part, churn can measure how sensitive your recommender system is to new user behavior.
cues.zh: 某種程度上，變動率能衡量推薦系統對新使用者行為有多敏感。

cues.en: If a user rates a new movie, does that substantially change their recommendations?
cues.zh: 如果使用者替一部新電影評分，推薦會有大幅變化嗎？

cues.en: If so, then your churn score will be high.
cues.zh: 如果會，變動率分數就會很高。

cues.en: Maybe just showing someone the same recommendations too many times is a bad idea in itself.
cues.zh: 或許反覆向同一個人展示相同推薦，本身就不是好主意。

cues.en: If a user keeps seeing the same recommendation but doesn't click on it, at some point should you just stop trying to recommend it and show the user something else instead?
cues.zh: 如果使用者一直看到相同推薦卻不點擊，是不是應該在某個時間停止推薦它，改展示其他東西？

cues.en: Sometimes a little bit of randomization in your top-N recommendations can keep them looking fresh, and expose your users to more items than they would have seen otherwise.
cues.zh: 有時在 Top-N 推薦中加入少量隨機性，能讓結果保持新鮮，讓使用者接觸到更多原本看不到的項目。

cues.en: But, just like diversity and novelty, high churn is not in itself a good thing.
cues.zh: 但就像多樣性與新穎性，高變動率本身並不是好事。

cues.en: You could maximize your churn metric by just recommending items completely at random, and of course, those would not be good recommendations.
cues.zh: 只要完全隨機推薦項目，就能把變動率指標拉到最高，但那些當然不是好的推薦。

cues.en: All of these metrics need to be looked at together, and you need to understand the trade-offs between them.
cues.zh: 這些指標必須一起觀察，也要了解彼此的取捨。

cues.en: One more metric is responsiveness; how quickly does new user behavior influence your recommendations?
cues.zh: 還有一個指標是反應速度，也就是新的使用者行為，多快會影響推薦？

cues.en: If you rate a new movie, does it affect your recommendations immediately or does it only affect your recommendations the next day after some nightly job runs?
cues.zh: 你替新電影評分後，推薦會立刻改變，還是得等到夜間批次工作執行後，隔天才改變？

cues.en: More responsiveness would always seem to be a good thing, but in the world of business you have to decide how responsive your recommender really needs to be, since recommender systems
cues.zh: 反應越快似乎總是越好，但在商業世界，必須決定推薦系統究竟需要多快回應，因為能夠

cues.en: that have instantaneous responsiveness are complex, difficult to maintain, and expensive to build.
cues.zh: 即時反應的推薦系統很複雜、難以維護，建立成本也很高。

cues.en: You need to strike your own balance between responsiveness and simplicity.
cues.zh: 你需要在反應速度與簡單性之間，找到自己的平衡。

cues.en: We've covered a lot of different ways to evaluate your recommender system; MAE, RMSE, Hit Rate in various forms, coverage, diversity, novelty, churn, and responsiveness.
cues.zh: 我們介紹了許多評估推薦系統的方式：MAE、RMSE、各種命中率、覆蓋率、多樣性、新穎性、變動率與反應速度。

cues.en: So how do you know what to focus on?
cues.zh: 那麼，怎麼知道該專注於哪個？

cues.en: Well, the answer is that it depends.
cues.zh: 答案是，要看情況。

cues.en: It may even depend on cultural factors.
cues.zh: 甚至可能取決於文化因素。

cues.en: Some cultures may want more diversity and novelty in their recommendations than others, while other cultures may want to stick with things that are familiar with them.
cues.zh: 有些文化比其他文化更希望推薦具備多樣性與新穎性，另一些文化則可能偏好熟悉的東西。

cues.en: It also depends on what you're trying to achieve as a business.
cues.zh: 也取決於企業想達成什麼目標。

cues.en: And usually, a business is just trying to make money, which leads to one more way to evaluate recommender systems that is arguably the most important of all.
cues.zh: 通常企業就是想賺錢，這就帶出另一種評估推薦系統的方法，可以說是最重要的方法。

cues.en: That's doing online A/B tests to tune your recommender system using your real customers, and measuring how they react to your recommendations.
cues.zh: 也就是用真實顧客進行線上 A/B 測試，調整推薦系統，衡量他們對推薦的反應。

cues.en: You can put recommendations from different algorithms in front of different sets of users, and measure if they actually buy, watch, or otherwise indicate interest in the recommendations you've presented.
cues.zh: 你可以向不同使用者群組呈現不同演算法產生的推薦，衡量他們是否真的購買、觀看，或以其他方式對推薦表達興趣。

cues.en: By always testing changes to your recommender system using controlled, online experiments, you can see if they actually cause people to discover and purchase more new things than they would have otherwise.
cues.zh: 持續透過受控的線上實驗，測試推薦系統的變更，就能知道這些變更是否真的讓人們發現並購買更多原本不會購買的新東西。

cues.en: That's ultimately what matters to your business, and it's ultimately what matters to your users, too.
cues.zh: 這才是最終對企業重要的事，對使用者也是如此。

cues.en: None of the metrics we've discussed matter more than how real customers react to the recommendations you produce in the real world.
cues.zh: 我們討論的任何指標，都不比真實顧客在真實世界對推薦的反應更重要。

cues.en: You can have the most accurate rating predictions in the world, but if customers can't find new items to buy or watch from your system, it will be worthless from a practical standpoint.
cues.zh: 即使你的評分預測是全世界最準確的，如果顧客無法透過系統找到想買、想看的新項目，從實務角度來看，它就毫無價值。

cues.en: If you test a new algorithm and it's more complex than the one it replaced, then you should discard it if it does not result in a measurable improvement in users interacting with the recommendations you present.
cues.zh: 如果測試新演算法，它比取代的舊演算法更複雜，卻沒有讓使用者與推薦的互動產生可衡量的改善，就應該捨棄它。

cues.en: Online tests can help you to avoid introducing complexity that adds no value, and remember, complex systems are difficult to maintain.
cues.zh: 線上測試能幫你避免引入沒有價值的複雜性，記得，複雜的系統很難維護。

cues.en: So remember, offline metrics such as accuracy, diversity, and novelty can all be indicators you can look at while developing recommender systems offline, but you should never declare victory
cues.zh: 因此，準確程度、多樣性、新穎性等離線指標，都可以作為離線開發推薦系統時的參考，但絕不要宣告成功，

cues.en: until you've measured a real impact on real users from your work.
cues.zh: 直到你衡量出工作成果對真實使用者造成了實際影響。

cues.en: Systems that look good in an offline setting often fail to have any impact in an online setting, that is, in the real world.
cues.zh: 離線看起來表現很好的系統，往往在線上，也就是真實世界，沒有任何影響。

cues.en: User behavior is the ultimate test of your work.
cues.zh: 使用者行為，才是工作成果的最終考驗。

cues.en: There is a real effect where often accuracy metrics tell you that an algorithm is great, only to have it do horribly in an online test.
cues.zh: 確實常出現這種現象：準確程度指標顯示演算法很好，結果線上測試卻表現很差。

cues.en: YouTube studied this, and calls it the "surrogate problem."
cues.zh: YouTube 研究過這件事，稱它為「代理問題」。

cues.en: Accurately predicted ratings don't necessarily make for good video recommendations.
cues.zh: 準確預測評分，不一定能產生好的影片推薦。

cues.en: YouTube said in one of their papers, and I quote, "There is more art than science "in selecting the surrogate problem for recommendations."
cues.zh: YouTube 在一篇論文中說，我引用一下：「為推薦選擇代理問題時，藝術成分多於科學。」

cues.en: What they mean is that you can't always use accuracy as a surrogate for good recommendations.
cues.zh: 意思是，你不能總把準確程度當成好的推薦的替代指標。

cues.en: Netflix came to the same conclusion, which is why they aren't really using the results of that one million dollar prize for accuracy that they paid out.
cues.zh: Netflix 也得到同樣結論，所以並沒有真正採用那場花了一百萬美元、以準確程度為目標的競賽成果。

cues.en: At the end of the day, the results of online A/B tests are the only evaluation that matters for your recommender system.
cues.zh: 說到底，線上 A/B 測試結果，才是推薦系統唯一真正重要的評估。

cues.en: Another thing you can do is just straight up ask your users if they think specific recommendations are good.
cues.zh: 你也可以直接問使用者，覺得某些推薦好不好。

cues.en: Just like you can ask for explicit feedback on items with ratings, you can ask users to rate your recommendations, too.
cues.zh: 就像能請使用者評分項目、提供明確回饋，也能請他們為推薦本身評分。

cues.en: This is called measuring the "perceived quality" of recommendations, and it seems like a good idea on paper, since, as you've learned, defining what makes a "good" recommendation is by no means clear.
cues.zh: 這叫做衡量推薦的「感知品質」，理論上似乎是好主意，因為如你所學，什麼叫「好」推薦，並不明確。

cues.en: In practice though, it's a tough thing to do.
cues.zh: 但實務上，這很難做。

cues.en: Users will probably be confused over whether you're asking them to rate the item or rate the recommendation, so you won't really know how to interpret this data.
cues.zh: 使用者可能搞不清楚，你要他評價項目，還是評價推薦，因此你也不會真正知道如何解讀資料。

cues.en: It also requires extra work from your customers with no clear payoff for them, so you're unlikely to get enough ratings on your recommendations to be useful.
cues.zh: 這也需要顧客額外付出心力，卻沒有明確回報，所以很難取得足夠、有用的推薦評分。

cues.en: It's best to just stick with online A/B tests, and measure how your customers vote with their wallets on the quality of your recommendations.
cues.zh: 最好還是採用線上 A/B 測試，衡量顧客如何用錢包，為推薦品質投票。
